analysis:
Examined all supplied patches, source excerpts and file metadata against the canonical definition index and selected details. release-dev-branch.yml replaces push releases with scheduled comparison and dev-only dispatch (head 37–41, 70–169, 173). The gate gains actions:write but executes no checked-out candidate code; API values are quoted and filenames are parsed as data. Its path list preserves the former filters, handles rename origins and conservatively dispatches on comparison errors, divergence or the 300-file cap. The reusable call retains environment=dev and inherited secrets (181–184). No supported authorization bypass or new plaintext/key exposure was identified; runtime encryption, caches, billing, fan/add-on/GPU controls are not changed in this scope.
release-provider.yml moves source resolution, qualification aggregation, staging and publication to GitHub Ubuntu runners (patch head 135, 304, 1211, 1320), retaining visible source/qualification dependencies and permissions, and caps signing at 90 minutes (343). No evidence establishes weaker artifact validation on those runners. Relevant contracts are A-005, A-011, A-017 and T-054: publication must remain distinct from durable serving qualification.
Integration must verify scripts/provider-release-resume.py and scripts/resolve-provider-release.sh accept workflow_dispatch on dev as a publishing dev-branch release. The supplied reusable BASE comments at 159–185 instead describe dispatch as master-checked/validation-only; implementations and any companion changes are absent, so incompatibility is not yet a finding. Also inspect release-provider.yml signing cleanup and publication transaction behavior under the newly enabled caller cancellation (release-dev-branch.yml:48–49) and signing timeout; publish-job serialization alone does not demonstrate cancellation safety. Staging/publication surrounding source beyond their patch hunks was not supplied. These are material cross-file integration questions, not proof of regressions or a full audit.
